01 What this is

The pitch,
plainly.

I'm turning forty next May. I was born in Hobart, haven't done the place proper justice in years, and a 40th seems like the right kind of excuse to fix that.

Four days hiking the Three Capes Track — the hut-to-hut one along Australia's tallest sea cliffs — then three nights back in town. MONA, Salamanca, long dinners that hopefully end worse than they start. Actual birthday lands on Saturday.

Hike not your thing? There's a toggle below. Hobart-only is a real option — fly in Thursday, leave Sunday, no backpack required.

One small thing: I'm picturing the hike as a boys' trip. Partners absolutely welcome for the Hobart half — but keen to keep the cliffs side a lads-only thing. If the consensus is to leave the Hobart section lads only too, we can do that. Tell me what you'd prefer.

04 Day by day

Seven days,
roughly like this.

Mon 10 MayDay 1
Hike

Fly south, then start walking

Earliest flight you can stomach into Hobart. Pick up the rental, drive 90 minutes south to Port Arthur, check in at the Three Capes office. Boat across to the trailhead, then a short 4km walk to Surveyors hut.

Tight day. Book the early flight — a delayed plane = missed boat = lost hike pass. Aim for the later afternoon boat to give yourself a buffer.

Skip if Hobart only

Tue 11 MayDay 2
Hike

Surveyors → Munro hut

11km along coastal cliffs and through eucalypt forest. Climb Arthurs Peak, look down at Cape Raoul. Sleep in Munro, which has a view that is genuinely wasted on bushwalkers.

Packs get lighter as we eat through the food.

Skip if Hobart only

Wed 12 MayDay 3
Hike

The Blade and Cape Pillar

The day I'll openly question all my life choices — 19km out to Cape Pillar and The Blade, the tallest sea cliffs in the southern hemisphere. Antarctica is the next thing south of you. Back to Retakunna for the night.

Drop the pack at the cape junction so you're not carrying everything for the side trip.

Skip if Hobart only

Thu 13 MayDay 4
Hike

Out via Cape Hauy to Fortescue Bay

14km via Mt Fortescue and (if your legs allow) Cape Hauy. Finish at the white-sand beach of Fortescue Bay — swim if you can stand the cold. Bus back to Port Arthur, then drive to Hobart.

Hot shower at the hotel that night will be the best you've ever had.

Skip if Hobart only — fly in this evening instead

Fri 14 MayDay 5
The big night

MONA, then the dinner

Catch the ferry from Brooke St Pier to MONA — Posh Pit upgrade for the wine and canapés en route. Three or four hours wandering the museum, lunch at Faro. Then the main event: dressed-up dinner at Fico or The Agrarian Kitchen. Bring an appetite and something nicer than a fleece.

For Hobart-only people: this is your first full day. If you want to bring a present, just turn up.

Sat 15 MayDay 6
The birthday

A chill day around Hobart

Slow start. Long brunch. Wander Salamanca markets, browse Battery Point's terraced lanes, drift through whatever bookshops, galleries, or wine bars catch your eye. Casual dinner at Templo or somewhere with small plates — deliberately easy on the head.

Actual birthday, but flying home Sunday means we're calling it early. No one wants to be the person at the airport in sunglasses.

Sun 16 MayDay 7
Travel

Brunch and home

Slow brunch at Pigeon Whole or wherever feels right. Afternoon flights home.

Or extend a day if you've got the leave to spare.

05 For the hikers

Pack light,
pack smart.

From the official Three Capes Track packing list. The huts have everything you'd need to survive — they don't have anything you'd want to wear or eat. Tasmania can throw four seasons at you in a day, so the list errs on the side of warm and dry.

12kg
Target pack weight

Including 2L of water. The lighter you pack, the more you'll enjoy it. Cotton and denim are out — they soak up water and won't dry.

3 huts
What's already at the huts

Bunks with mattress (no pillow), gas cooktops with self-ignition, pots and pans, rainwater tanks, soap, USB charging, drying line. Bring everything else.

!
Biosecurity

Tassie is keeping out root rot, frog fungus, and weed seeds. Check, clean, and dry boots before flying. Use the washdown stations at Denmans Cove and the Cape Pillar junction.

06 What it'll cost you

The big rocks,
roughly.

Approximate, in AUD, per person. Just the three big-ticket items so you can see the shape of it — food, drinks, ground transport, MONA, and so on are extra (and entirely up to you). Solo rooms throughout. The ~$400/night assumes the higher end (MACq 01 etc.) — I'm chasing a group rate that should bring it down, and there are cheaper places if needed.

On top of that

  • Food & drinksBudget what you'd normally spend. Track food $80, Hobart dinners $80–200 a pop if you're going hard.
  • Hire car & petrolSplittable. Negligible if we're sharing, $300+ if you're solo.
  • MONA, ferries, taxisMaybe $150 across the trip.
  • Travel insurance$50–100. Recommended.
  • Gear (hikers only)$200–1,500 depending on what you already own.

Here's the order
of operations.

01

Tell me you're in

A 'yes' or even a 'probably' will do — I'll take what I can get. Need to know by mid-2026 to lock the Three Capes hut booking. Passes go on sale 13 months ahead and they sell.

Deadline: 14 May 2026
02

I'll book the hike

Once we have a number, I'll book the Three Capes pass for the group. You transfer me $650 and we're in.

By: July 2026
03

Book your own flights

Melbourne ↔ Hobart, Mon 10 May → Sun 16 May (full trip) or Thu 13 May → Sun 16 May (Hobart only). Full-trip people: book the earliest morning flight you can. Lock by August 2026 for decent fares.

By: Aug 2026
04

Hotel + restaurants

I'll send a group spreadsheet so we're in the same place. Birthday dinner needs booking by mid-Feb 2027 — Fico goes fast.

By: Feb 2027

A yes, a maybe, or a "nope, but I'll buy you a beer when you're back" — any of those is a fine answer.
